ultimate.title: Solve the Skewb Puzzleball
ultimate.intro: Work through the four main corners, the four movable corners, then the six broad roof pieces. The expandable move tables cover every case, with the exact ring letters used in this game.
notation: A letter is one 120° clockwise turn, viewed directly from outside that turning side. A prime (′) reverses it. Use Notation moves and the Inverse checkbox to enter the sequences exactly. The ring arrows describe motion on the ring map.

L, R, D, B are the four main controls used by this guide. Lowercase l, r, d, b turn the opposite halves; they are not small tips. Dragging the 3D view only changes your viewpoint and never renames a control.

Enable Piece labels. A label such as LR → RD means “the piece belonging at LR is now at RD.” A single LR means it is in its own slot, but it may still need orienting. Turn the view to expose labels on hidden pieces.

Two-letter slots lie between the named uppercase axes: LR is between L and R. Three-letter slots lie opposite the omitted axis: RDB is opposite L. Within a slot name, the letter order does not matter. The letters printed inside a move sequence do matter.

The broad four-sticker pieces are called roofs here. Opposite roofs can have the same four colors, but the order of those colors differs. Piece labels distinguish their destinations while you learn the pattern.

steps.title: 1 · Set the guide frame
steps.body:
A fresh Randomize already uses this frame. If you have used lowercase turns, check that the four main pieces L, R, D and B are back at their same-letter positions. Use Piece labels; this step restores their locations without unscrambling the puzzle.

First bring the piece named L to slot L:

L piece is now atDo
LNothing
RB b′
DR r′
BD d′

Then keep L there and bring the piece named R to slot R:

R piece is now atDo
RNothing
DL′ l
BL l′

All four main pieces should now have single-letter labels. These paired turns deliberately rotate the entire puzzle; perform both moves. From here onward, use only the uppercase controls shown in the guide.

steps.title: 2 · Orient the four main corners
steps.body:
The main corners L, R, D and B remain in their slots throughout the uppercase-only solve. Their three stickers establish the color scheme for every other piece.

  1. Turn L and R until their two blue stickers lie on opposite, parallel faces.
  2. Turn D until its gold sticker lies on the opposite face from the gold sticker of L.
  3. Turn B until its emerald sticker lies on the opposite face from the emerald sticker of L.

All six color pairs on these four corners should now occupy opposite faces. Rotate your view to check them. Each main turn changes only its own main corner’s orientation, so the later adjustments preserve the earlier ones.

steps.title: 3 · Place the four movable corners
steps.body:
Inspect RDB, LDB, LRB and LRD. Ignore their twists. If every piece is in its own slot, continue. Otherwise the four pieces form two exchanged pairs; choose the row matching those pairs.

Exchange these pairsPerform once
LDB ↔ RDB
LRB ↔ LRD		L D L′ D′ L D L′ D′ L D L′ D′
LDB ↔ LRD
LRB ↔ RDB		L B L′ B′ L B L′ B′ L B L′ B′

LRD ↔ RDB		L R L′ R′ L R L′ R′ L R L′ R′

Run the whole sequence before checking. The movable corners should now be in their own slots. The roof pieces and all four main corners stay as they were. If the labels show a three-piece cycle instead of two exchanges, recheck the main-corner orientations in step 2.

steps.title: 4 · Twist the movable corners in pairs
steps.body:
Use the solved main corners as the color references. A correctly oriented movable corner extends the colors of its three neighboring faces. Choose two corners that still need twisting.

Each row turns its first listed corner clockwise and its second counterclockwise, viewed directly from outside each corner. If your chosen first corner needs the opposite turn, perform the row twice. This fixes that corner; the partner may still need work. Repeat with two remaining twisted corners until all eight corners match.

These sequences keep every corner in its slot and preserve the four main corners. They can move the roofs, which you solve next. If exactly one corner appears twisted, recheck the others before continuing.

steps.title: 5 · Put the six roofs in their slots
steps.body:
Ignore roof orientation for this step. Use the labels to put all six four-sticker pieces at their destinations: LR, LD, LB, RD, RB, DB. This is helpful where opposite pieces share a set of colors.

Choose a useful cycle: find a misplaced piece. Call its current slot A and its destination B. Look at the piece currently at B and call its destination C. If C is A, choose any other misplaced slot for C. Move A → B → C → A, then inspect again. This places at least one piece correctly each time.

Find the row containing those three slots. Its arrows show where the pieces currently in those slots will travel. If you need the reverse direction, perform that entire row twice. A cycle can be read starting at any of its three slots.

steps.title: 6 · Flip the remaining roofs
steps.body:
A roof in its correct slot has two possible orientations. It is solved when all four stickers continue their neighboring face colors. The number of incorrect roofs is even.

Choose any two incorrect roofs and use their row below. It flips both pieces in place and leaves every other piece unchanged. Repeat with the remaining incorrect pairs.
